crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Resection Planning and Margins
children.blurb: Resection planning and margins covers the work of deciding, before and during an operation, how much tissue to remove and where the cut should run.

children.name: Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery
children.blurb: Haptic feedback in robotic surgery is the deliberate return of touch sensation to a surgeon who is operating through a machine rather than with their hands directly.

children.name: Virtual Surgical Rehearsal
children.blurb: Virtual surgical rehearsal is the practice of building a patient specific model of the anatomy and the planned operation, then running the procedure in simulation before anyone enters the operating room.

children.name: Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery
children.blurb: Tremor stabilisation in microsurgery covers the systems and techniques that suppress involuntary hand movement during procedures on structures only a millimetre or two across, such as vessel, nerve and eye surgery.

children.name: Remote Telesurgery
children.blurb: Remote telesurgery covers operations in which the surgeon is not in the same room as the patient, working through a robotic platform that carries hand motion, vision and sometimes force feedback across a network.

sections.body: Surgical robotics and navigation covers the machines, software and imaging that sit between a surgeon and a patient's tissue. Artificial intelligence is not operating on anyone. It is doing narrower jobs: segmenting tumours on scans so a resection line can be drawn before the patient is on the table, filtering the hand movements that reach the instrument tip, and predicting how a planned cut will deform the surrounding anatomy. In telesurgery it helps compensate for the delay between a surgeon's console and a robot in another city. The common thread is augmentation, where the machine handles geometry, timing and steadiness while the human keeps judgement and control.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature. Tremor filtering is essentially a solved control problem, and robotic platforms with motion scaling are routine in many hospitals. Resection planning from imaging is well established as decision support, though its accuracy depends on the scan and on how much the tissue shifts once surgery begins. Haptic feedback remains the hardest problem, because sensing force at a small tip and returning it faithfully to a console is a hardware and latency challenge as much as a software one. Virtual rehearsal is promising but still limited by how well a model matches a specific patient. Telesurgery works over short distances and controlled links, and long distance work is constrained by network delay and by who carries legal responsibility when the surgeon is not in the room.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages run roughly in the order a case unfolds. Resection Planning and Margins is the starting point, covering how imaging and models define what to remove and what to spare. Virtual Surgical Rehearsal takes that plan and lets a surgeon practise it on a patient specific model before the real operation. Haptic Feedback in Robotic Surgery addresses what the surgeon feels during the work, and Tremor Stabilisation in Microsurgery addresses how steady the instrument is once it is inside the body. Remote Telesurgery is the outlier, because it changes where the surgeon stands rather than what the tools do, and it pulls together the planning, feedback and stabilisation questions under the added strain of distance and delay. A reader new to the area should start with resection planning, then move to rehearsal, and treat the haptic and tremor pages as the engineering core, with telesurgery as the systems level view.
